Decomposed Whale Carcass Closes Two Popular Sydney Beaches

30 Oct 2026, 02:22 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Climate Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

Image: www.theguardian.com — Creative Commons

Share this article
WhatsAppFacebookTelegram
Key takeaways Beach Closures Following Thursday Discovery Two popular beaches in Sydney's eastern suburbs were temporarily closed to the public on Thursday morning after a decomposing whale carcass washed ashore. The marine mammal's body was discovered at Lurline Bay, a rocky cove

Beach Closures Following Thursday Discovery

Two popular beaches in Sydney's eastern suburbs were temporarily closed to the public on Thursday morning after a decomposing whale carcass washed ashore. The marine mammal's body was discovered at Lurline Bay, a rocky cove defined by surrounding cliffs located within the Randwick local government area.

Footage released by Randwick City Council captures the large carcass floating in the coastal waters of the Sydney bay. Local authorities moved quickly to restrict public access to nearby swimming areas as a safety precaution while managing the unusual marine incident.

Identification and Initial Assessment

Preliminary observations suggest the animal is a juvenile humpback whale. Due to the advanced state of decomposition noted by officials, the exact cause of death and the timeline of how the carcass drifted into the rocky cove remain under ongoing assessment by marine authorities.

Randwick City Council and local lifeguards implemented the beach closures at Maroubra and Coogee to manage public health risks and facilitate coordination for the eventual removal of the marine mammal.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

For residents and visitors planning trips to Sydney's eastern beaches, local authorities advise checking real-time council updates before visiting coastal areas, as temporary closures may remain active during cleanup and removal operations.

Readers can verify official updates and view the council-released footage directly through the [Guardian Environmental Coverage](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/video/2026/oct/22/whale-carcass-closes-maroubra-and-coogee-beaches-in-sydney-video).
